judge_verdict.summary: The agent fully executed the Film Production Day adaptability workflow, but the verifier failed it for one extra confirmation email that strict tool-count matching treats as an automatic zero.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the agent genuinely completed the adaptability scenario, but the LLM action judge scored reward 0 because of a strict tool-count gate [10][11]. The verifier reported binary_reward 0 [1], and this task is graded in adaptability action mode—matching the agent's write-tool calls against eleven oracle actions covering initial Saturday booking plus the reschedule branch [3][4][5]. The user asked to cancel upcoming-Saturday appointments, schedule "Film Production Day" 8 AM–8 PM with the Film Producer friend, email him the details, notify when done, and if he cannot make Saturday accept his proposed alternative while cancelling conflicting appointments that day [2]. The agent identified Åke Lindström, deleted the Saturday Brand Partnership Meeting (f041377cce14424692cf96b15fc4fd0b), created the Saturday event with correct title, times, and attendee, and emailed him the appointment details [6][7]. It then waited for Åke's reply, read his counterproposal of Thursday October 17 at the same time, deleted all five Thursday appointments plus the original Saturday Film Production Day, and rescheduled the event to 2024-10-17 08:00:00–20:00:00 with Åke as attendee—matching every oracle calendar delete ID and both add-calendar-event payloads [8][9]. The only substantive deviation from the oracle trace is a second send_email after rescheduling confirming the new Thursday date [9], which makes agent EmailClientApp__send_email count 2 versus oracle 1 while all calendar tool counts already align; the verifier allows one extra send_message_to_user but applies no similar tolerance to email and forces reward to 0.0 on any per-tool count mismatch [10][11]. That extra confirmation is reasonable given the interaction and does not leave the task unfulfilled—the final calendar state and adaptability handling match what the reference solution accomplishes—so the FAIL is a verifier strictness artifact, not an agent miss.

verdicts.verifier_or_task_concern: The adaptability verifier applies a hard zero reward on any per-tool write-count mismatch; it tolerates one extra send_message_to_user but not an extra send_email, so a fully correct calendar/email workflow that includes a reasonable post-reschedule confirmation email is scored as complete failure despite matching all required oracle calendar operations.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent completed the initial Saturday booking but never handled the friend's counter-proposal reschedule to Thursday, so the verifier's FAIL is correct.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN): the held-out adaptability judge scored reward 0.0 because the agent's write-action log could not match the eleven-action oracle sequence [1][3]. The user request required booking Film Production Day on the upcoming Saturday, canceling conflicting appointments, emailing the Stockholm film-producer friend, reporting completion, and then—if the friend cannot make Saturday—accepting his proposed alternative, canceling conflicts on that day, and rescheduling the event [2][4]. The agent did execute the opening phase correctly: it deleted the Saturday Brand Partnership Meeting, created Film Production Day on 2024-10-19 with Åke Lindström as attendee, and sent him an email at ake.lindstrom@filmproduktion.se [5]. After that it spent many turns calling are_wait_for_notification, but every wait returned empty notifications and the simulation eventually exited with loop_dead without any reply from Åke ever appearing in the trajectory [6]. The reference solution's adaptability branch deletes the Saturday Film Production Day, clears five Thursday appointments, and recreates Film Production Day on 2024-10-17 08:00–20:00 once the environment event fires [2]; the agent performed none of those seven follow-on writes, its final calendar check still showed only the Saturday event, and it nonetheless sent the user a Done message claiming the work was finished [7][8]. With only four successful writes versus eleven oracle writes, the action-mode tool-count gate alone forces reward 0 even before semantic mismatches in the email subject and completion wording, so the agent did not genuinely solve this hard adaptability scenario.

def _check_tool_call_counts(
    oracle_actions: list[NormalizedAction],
    agent_actions: list[NormalizedAction],
) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, Any]]:
    aui_tool = "AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user"
    oracle_counter = Counter(action.canonical_tool for action in oracle_actions)
    agent_counter = Counter(action.canonical_tool for action in agent_actions)

    oracle_aui_count = oracle_counter.pop(aui_tool, 0)
    agent_aui_count = agent_counter.pop(aui_tool, 0)
    counts_match = (
        oracle_counter == agent_counter
        and oracle_aui_count
        <= agent_aui_count
        <= oracle_aui_count + EXTRA_SEND_MESSAGE_TO_USER_ALLOWED
    )

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure (FN): the adaptability verifier recorded reward 0.0 [1] even though the agent genuinely accomplished the Film Production Day scenario described in the user prompt [2]. The task required cancelling Saturday appointments, scheduling an all-day event with the Stockholm film-producer friend, emailing appointment details, notifying the user, and—if the friend counter-proposes—accepting the new slot while clearing conflicts and rescheduling [2], and the agent executed that path by deleting the Saturday conflict, creating "Film Production Day" on 2024-10-19 08:00–20:00 with Åke Lindström, sending the notification email, and updating the user [6], then waiting for Åke's reply proposing Thursday October 17 at the same time [7], deleting all five Thursday conflicts plus the original Saturday event, and recreating "Film Production Day" on 2024-10-17 08:00–20:00 before sending a follow-up user update [8]. Because this task's config is adaptability, the verifier runs in action-mode and compares write-tool traces against the oracle [3]; it sets reward to zero whenever write-tool counts diverge from the oracle, regardless of how many individual actions would otherwise match [4], requiring exact counter equality aside from at most one extra send_message_to_user [5]. The agent's additional Emails__reply_to_email acknowledging the reschedule [9] is absent from the eleven-action oracle reference [9], so oracle_counter and agent_counter differ and the scorer returns tool_call_count_mismatch with reward 0.0 even though that reply is optional relative to the user request and the core calendar/email/adaptability requirements were met [1][4][5][9].
